chunks.area: electron/worktrees.js — isTransientWorktree + the transient split in gcScanInner
chunks.rationale: The whole change is here. A worktree is transient when its thread is archived or was created by a fork (handoffFrom). Transient dirs are dropped straight into retentionDrop instead of competing for a keep-N slot, so the buffer now holds only the user's own settled threads. The unmerged grace lives in the same branch: a transient dir with commits the base branch lacks waits UNMERGED_GRACE_MS (3 days) from threadActivityAt before it becomes a candidate.
risks: isTransientWorktree matches every handoffFrom thread, not only orchWorker forks — a provider handoff thread counts too. Deliberate (it is still a fork), but it means a user-facing thread's worktree loses the keep-N buffer once it settles.
isSettledForGc returns true for archived BEFORE the prState check, so an archived thread with an OPEN PR is transient. Safe only because a PR implies the branch is pushed.

inspections[i] is read inside the settled loop; it is the parallel array built above, not re-derived. An unreadable dir yields unmerged=0 and becomes a candidate, but gcClean still refuses it via `blocked`.

chunks.rationale: The scan decides; enforceRetention only has to stop vetoing. `c.transient === true || !(c.unmerged > 0)` keeps the #601 guard for everything else. The `configured` gate is untouched, so worktreeRetention: 0 is still a full opt-out.
risks: The flag is set from transientDrop membership, so a transient dir that was held back by the grace period carries no flag — correct, but it means `transient` on a candidate reads as 'reclaimable now', not 'is a fork'.

chunks.rationale: This file's whole fixture was addArchivedWorker, so it encoded the old policy and six tests failed on the new one. Added addSettledThread for the keep-N cases and re-pointed the buffer tests at it; the archived-worker cases now assert the opposite (all twelve drop). Read the diff for what the contract used to be.
risks: 'archiving a thread reclaims its own merged-out worktree' is a behaviour change users will feel first: archiving a clean thread now deletes its checkout immediately, not once the project exceeds ten.

chunks.rationale: New cases for the fork path and the grace window, plus one that pins the #601 guard for non-transient unmerged worktrees so this change cannot quietly widen later.
risks: The grace tests use real Date.now() offsets rather than an injected clock; they are direction-only (fresh vs 4 days old) so they cannot flake on timing, but they do rely on the constant staying at 3 days.

chunks.rationale: Type for the new flag, GC dialog pre-ticks transient rows (background retention takes them anyway, so leaving them unticked would misrepresent what happens), and the retention field's help text no longer implies forks occupy a slot.
risks: Pre-ticking an unmerged row in the batch dialog is a deliberate softening of #601's 'never part of select all' rule — it only applies to transient rows.

Policy change, not a bug fix: on the reporter's live store this reclaims 19.9 GB of 29 GB at the next boot sweep. Verified by a read-only gcScan against a copy of the real coder-store.json — 27 transient candidates, 2 blocked as dirty, no working or pinned thread touched.

GC removes directories only and never branches, so unmerged worker commits stay reachable by branch name. But gcClean nulls thread.worktreePath AND thread.branch, so the thread no longer points at its own work — recovery means finding coder/<slug>-<threadShortId> by hand. That is pre-existing behaviour, now reachable for unmerged forks.
